title: A Closer Look at the Macula

patient.name: Mdm Wong Siew Lan
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for Cirrus OCT macular scan — distortion of vision in left eye

history.hpc: Mdm Wong noticed that straight lines, such as door frames and tiles, appear wavy when she looks at them with her left eye over the past 2 weeks. She has no pain. Her right eye vision feels normal to her. The doctor examined her fundus and noted some changes at the macula in the left eye, and has ordered a Cirrus OCT macular scan to evaluate the retinal layers in detail.
history.pmhx: Hypertension. No previous eye surgery. Wears reading glasses for near work.
history.family_hx: Mother had 'macular degeneration' and lost central vision in old age

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Mild nuclear sclerosis bilaterally, otherwise unremarkable
examination_findings.fundus: Right eye: normal macula. Left eye: drusen and pigmentary changes at macula, doctor notes possible subretinal fluid

investigations.amsler_grid: Left eye: patient reports wavy distortion of horizontal lines near central area. Right eye: grid appears normal.

cirrus_oct_right.result: Normal foveal contour, no fluid or oedema

cirrus_oct_left.result: Subretinal fluid and intraretinal cystic changes at the macula, drusen present

diagnosis: Cirrus OCT macular scan completed bilaterally. Left eye shows increased central subfield thickness with subretinal fluid and intraretinal cysts, consistent with the doctor's suspicion of exudative age-related macular degeneration, for further review and possible referral to medical retina.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and confirm both eyes are to be scanned
Explain the procedure to patient: non-contact, sits at a machine, looks at a green fixation light, takes about 5 minutes
Set up the Cirrus OCT machine, enter patient details accurately
Position patient comfortably at chinrest with forehead against the rest, adjust table height
Select the macular cube scan protocol as ordered by the doctor
Ask patient to keep both eyes open and fixate steadily on the green target, blinking normally between captures
Check signal strength for each scan (aim for signal strength 7/10 or higher) — repeat scan if signal is poor or patient blinked during capture
Review scan for obvious motion artefacts or eye movement and rescan if needed
Print/export report showing retinal thickness map and cross-sectional images, hand to doctor
follow_up: Doctor to review OCT findings and correlate with fundus examination and Amsler grid result
If exudative AMD confirmed, patient may be referred urgently to medical retina for consideration of intravitreal injection
Repeat OCT at follow-up to monitor response to treatment
patient_education: Explain that this scan takes detailed pictures of the layers at the back of the eye, near where she sees the wavy lines
Tell patient the test is quick, painless, and does not touch the eye
Advise patient to monitor her vision at home with the Amsler grid and report any sudden worsening promptly, as this may need urgent treatment

key_points: Confirms patient identity and confirms both eyes are to be scanned
Elicits the symptom of metamorphopsia (wavy lines) and which eye is affected
Asks about family history of macular degeneration as a relevant risk factor
Explains the non-contact nature of the OCT procedure to the patient
Sets up Cirrus OCT machine correctly with accurate patient details and selects the macular cube protocol
Positions patient correctly at chinrest and obtains steady fixation
Checks signal strength for each scan and repeats scans with poor signal or motion artefact
Records central subfield thickness and qualitative findings (fluid, cysts, drusen) for both eyes
Recognises that increased central subfield thickness with subretinal/intraretinal fluid suggests macular pathology
Understands the purpose of OCT: detailed cross-sectional imaging of retinal layers at the macula
Does not diagnose AMD independently — reports findings to doctor
Correlates Amsler grid distortion with the affected eye on OCT
Documents central subfield thickness and signal strength for both eyes accurately
Hands report promptly to doctor, especially given suspicion of exudative AMD requiring urgent review
Educates patient on home Amsler grid monitoring and when to seek urgent review
Ensures good quality scans before ending the session
